questions.stem: The box lists some substances. Choose substances from the box to answer these questions. Each substance may be used once, more than once or not at all.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name a metallic element.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name a compound.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name a mixture.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Name an element that is a gas at room temperature.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Name an element that forms a basic oxide.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Name two elements that are in the same group of the Periodic Table.

questions.stem: A student does a chromatography experiment using ink 1, ink 2, and three known dyes A, B and C. The student uses water as the solvent. The diagram shows the student's chromatogram.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Deduce what conclusions can be made about the composition of ink 1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one conclusion that can be made about ink 2.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Suggest how the student could change the experiment to find the composition of ink 2.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the $ R_{f} $ value of dye C, giving your answer to 2 significant figures.

questions.stem: Crude oil is a mixture of organic compounds. Most of these compounds are members of the same homologous series.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the name of this homologous series.

parts.label: b
parts.text: An industrial process is used to separate crude oil into fractions.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: The process depends on a difference in a property of the fractions. What is this property? A boiling point B density melting point D solubility

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: The boxes give some uses of fractions and some names of fractions. Draw one straight line from each use to its correct fraction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Fuels obtained from the fractions may contain impurities. Explain how the combustion of a common impurity in fuels may cause an environmental problem.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Some of the fractions contain long-chain molecules which are not very useful.

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Give the name of the process used to convert long-chain molecules into more useful shorter-chain molecules.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Give the catalyst and temperature used in the industrial process to convert long-chain molecules into shorter-chain molecules. catalyst temperature

parts.label: d-iii
parts.text: When $ C_{1 3} H_{2 8} $ is used in this process, three different molecules are formed. Complete the equation for this reaction. $\mathrm {C} _ {1 3} \mathrm {H} _ {2 8} \rightarrow \mathrm {C} _ {8} \mathrm {H} _ {1 8} +$

questions.stem: When iron is left in damp air, rust forms on its surface.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the chemical name for rust.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Explain how a barrier method prevents rusting.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A student uses this apparatus to find the approximate percentage by volume of oxygen in air. This is the student's method. place a graduated glass tube in a beaker of water place some damp iron wool and a rubber bung in the top of the tube record the reading of the water level in the tube leave the apparatus for a few days record the reading of the water level again The diagram shows the readings at the start and at the end of the experiment. start end

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Use the readings to complete the table, giving all values to the nearest $ 0. 5 \mathrm{c m}^{3}. $

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: The student uses these results to calculate the percentage by volume of oxygen in air. Suggest why her calculated value is lower than the expected value.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The student repeats the experiment using the same apparatus. These are her results for the second experiment. volume of air in tube at start = 80.0 $ cm^{3} $ reading at start=20.0 reading at end=35.5 Use the results to calculate the percentage by volume of oxygen in air.

questions.stem: A student uses this apparatus to investigate the effect of heat on different solid metal carbonates. This is the student's method. use a spatula to put some metal carbonate in the boiling tube fit the delivery tube into position pour some limewater into the test tube start a timer and immediately begin to heat the metal carbonate record the time when a change first occurs in the limewater The student repeats the method using different metal carbonates. When a metal carbonate is heated a reaction sometimes occurs. The equation for the reaction is $\mathrm {m e t a l c a r b o n a t e} \rightarrow \mathrm {m e t a l o x i d e} + \mathrm {c a r b o n d i o x i d e}$

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the name given to this type of reaction.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State two variables that the student should control in this investigation.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why bubbles appear in the limewater immediately after heating has started but before there is any change to the metal carbonate.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Explain the purpose of limewater in this investigation.

parts.label: e
parts.text: The table shows some of the results for the student's investigation.

parts.label: e-i
parts.text: State the colour change that occurs for copper(II) carbonate.

parts.label: e-ii
parts.text: Give a chemical equation for this reaction of copper(II) carbonate.

parts.label: f
parts.text: There is a relationship between the position of a metal in the reactivity series and how easily the metal carbonate reacts when heated. Use the student's results and your own knowledge to deduce this relationship.

parts.label: f-ii
parts.text: State how you should extend the investigation to see if your deduction is correct.

questions.stem: Zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form hydrogen.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give a chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Give a test for hydrogen gas.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A student investigates the reaction between pieces of zinc and dilute hydrochloric acid. In each experiment, he uses the same mass of zinc but a different volume of the acid. He collects the hydrogen and measures its volume in each experiment. The graph shows the student's results. Volume of hydrogen in $ \mathrm{c m}^{3} $

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Use the graph to find the minimum volume of acid needed to react with all of the zinc.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: The student repeats the investigation, using hydrochloric acid of double the original concentration. Determine the volume of hydrogen that would be collected using $ 1 5 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of this acid. Show your working on the graph.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain how increasing the concentration of the hydrochloric acid affects the rate of reaction.

parts.label: d
parts.text: The rate of reaction could also be affected by changing the temperature of the hydrochloric acid, or by using a catalyst. Explain one other way in which the rate of reaction between zinc and hydrochloric acid can be affected.

questions.stem: The formation of ions and covalent bonds involves electrons. The table gives the electronic configurations of atoms of hydrogen, lithium and chlorine.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe the different roles of electrons in the formation of ions in lithium chloride covalent bonds in hydrogen chloride

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why lithium chloride has a higher melting point than hydrogen chloride. Refer to structure and bonding in your answer.

questions.stem: (a) (i) Organic compounds can exist as isomers. Explain what is meant by the term isomers. (ii) Organic compound Q reacts with bromine, without the presence of ultraviolet radiation, to form the compound $ \mathrm{C_{4} H_{8} B r_{2}} $ Draw the displayed formulae of two isomers of Q.

parts.label: b
parts.text: An acrylic polymer can be formed from molecules with this structure.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: A student describes the molecule as an unsaturated hydrocarbon Explain whether this is a correct description.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Name the type of polymerisation that occurs in the formation of the polymer.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: Complete the equation for the polymerisation reaction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Octane is a compound in petrol. The equation for the complete combustion of octane is $\mathrm {C} _ {8} \mathrm {H} _ {1 8} + 1 2. 5 \mathrm {O} _ {2} \rightarrow 8 \mathrm {C O} _ {2} + 9 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: The fuel tank of a car contains $ 5 0. 0 \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ of octane. Calculate the mass, in kg, of carbon dioxide formed if all the octane in the fuel tank undergoes complete combustion. [mass of 1 dm $ ^{3} $ of octane=700 g]

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: State an environmental problem caused by carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: Lithium, sodium and potassium are the first three elements in Group 1 of the Periodic Table. (a) Suggest why these three elements are all stored in paraffin oil.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Caesium, Cs, is below potassium in Group 1.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Give a similarity and a difference between the reactions of potassium with water and caesium with water. similarity. difference.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Give the chemical equation for the reaction between caesium and water.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A student investigates the temperature change in the reaction between dilute acids and solutions of Group 1 hydroxides. He uses this apparatus. This is the student's method. measure the temperature of $ 5 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of hydrochloric acid pour the acid into a polystyrene cup add $ 5 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of sodium hydroxide solution to the acid measure the maximum temperature of the mixture

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Suggest what could be added to the apparatus to improve the experiment.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Explain a change to the method that would improve the accuracy of the experiment.

parts.label: d
parts.text: These are the student's results. $\begin{array}{l} \mathrm {t e m p e r a t u r e o f h y d r o c h l o r i c a c i d} = 1 9. 9 ^ {\circ} \mathrm {C} \\ \mathrm {m a x i m u m t e m p e r a t u r e o f m i x t u r e} = 2 6. 5 ^ {\circ} \mathrm {C} \\ \end{array}$

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Calculate the energy change, Q, in joules for this reaction. [mass of $ 1. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of mixture $ = 1. 0 \mathrm{g} $] [for the mixture, c=4.2 J/g/ $ ^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $]

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: In the student's reaction between hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide, 0.050mol of water forms. Calculate the molar enthalpy change, $ \Delta H $ , in kJ/mol for this reaction. $\Delta H =$

parts.label: a
parts.text: Soluble salts can be prepared by the reaction between a metal oxide and an acid. The equation for this type of reaction is $\mathrm {m e t a l o x i d e} + \mathrm {a c i d} \rightarrow \mathrm {s a l t} + \mathrm {w a t e r}$

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: State the name given to this type of reaction.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: State, in terms of protons, what happens in this reaction.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A student is given $ 5 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of dilute sulfuric acid and a bottle of solid copper(II) carbonate. Describe the method that the student should use to prepare a saturated solution of copper(II) sulfate. In your answer, refer to the pieces of apparatus that the student should use.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: The student produces dry crystals of hydrated copper(II) sulfate from the saturated solution. He calculates that 6.40 g of dry crystals should be formed. The mass of dry crystals he actually obtains is 1.80 g less than he calculated. Calculate the student's percentage yield. Give your answer to one decimal place.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Gypsum is hydrated calcium sulfate. A sample of gypsum contains 79% of calcium sulfate by mass. Calculate the value of x in $ \mathrm{C a S O_{4}. x H_{2}O} $ [ $ M_{\mathrm{r}} $ of $ \mathrm{C a S O_{4}}=1 3 6 $ $ M_{\mathrm{r}} $ of $ \mathrm{H_{2}O}=1 8 ] $

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Describe a test for calcium ions in the sample of gypsum.
